description:
Part of epic ag-o6z; read it first. Needs ag-o6z.1, ag-o6z.2 (GitHubStartedAt/GitHubCompletedAt) and ag-o6z.3 (Jobs). The trailer comes from ag-o6z.6.

## Goal

Agbredo records the PRs that agents open, links each to the run that opened it with a stated confidence, and records rule breaks as findings. It does NOT follow what people do with the PR later (merged, closed, reopened): that is agent performance evaluation, a separate epic (decision with Matt, 2026-10-15). An agent that does not follow the trailer rule must still leave a trace.

## Before coding: ask Matt to change the GitHub App

Matt does this by hand: in the App settings add the permission "Pull requests: Read-only" and subscribe to the "Pull request" event; then accept the new permission on each installation. Until then no pull_request deliveries arrive.

## Rules

Which PRs are recorded in Postgres: `pull_request` deliveries with action `opened` (also `edited`, only to refresh title/body/trailer while the PR is unlinked; `closed`, `reopened` and other actions are `ignored`), for a repository that has at least one live deployment (any workflow file), and where `pull_request.user.type == "Bot"` OR the body contains a trailer. Everything else: outcome `ignored` (the raw delivery is archived anyway; human PRs stay only there).

Trailer: a line in the PR body matching `^Agbredo-Run: ([0-9]+)/([0-9]+)\s*$` (multiline): GitHub run ID / run attempt. ag-o6z.6 adds it to open-pr.sh (done, released in pipelines v1). The body above the trailer is written by Claude and may contain fake trailer lines: use the LAST matching line only.

Link levels, decided when the PR is first seen, re-tried while unlinked (see below), never changed once declared or inferred:
- declared: trailer present; author is a bot; `head.repo.full_name` equals `base.repo.full_name`; Agbredo has a run in this repository (any deployment) with that GitHub run ID and attempt; and `pull_request.created_at` lies in [run GitHubStartedAt (or CreatedAt), GitHubCompletedAt + 60 s] (open end if still running).
- inferred: no valid trailer, author is a bot, and exactly one Agbredo run in this repository has that window around `created_at`.
- unlinked: anything else, with a reason: `no_run_in_window`, `several_runs_in_window` (keep the candidate run IDs), `trailer_run_unknown`, `trailer_outside_window`, `trailer_from_fork`, `trailer_by_human`.

Findings, stored on the PR record and shown:
- `missing_trailer`: inferred link (the pipeline opened a PR without the rule).
- `trailer_mismatch`: a trailer is present but the link is not declared (reason as above).
- `unlinked_bot_pr`: a bot PR in a watched repository linked to no run.

Known limits, to write in the design doc: `github-actions[bot]` is also the author for ordinary CI automation, so inferred links can be wrong (that is why they are labelled). An agent that opens a PR with a person's token looks like that person and is not recorded in Postgres.

## Storage

Migration (next free number): table `pull_requests`: `id text PRIMARY KEY` (`<repository id>:<number>`), `owner text`, `repository text`, `number int`, `run_id text NULL REFERENCES runs(id)`, `link text NOT NULL` (declared / inferred / unlinked), `document jsonb NOT NULL` (title, html_url, author login and type, head ref, head repo, base ref, created_at, trailer as found, link reason, candidate runs, findings; facts as at opening, no later state), `updated_at timestamptz`. Index on run_id, and on (lower(owner), lower(repository)).
The `opened` delivery also adds an Event to the linked run (Type `github.pull_request`, Action opened, stable ID from the delivery ID). Later PR changes are not recorded in Postgres (they stay in the raw archive).
Ordering: a PR delivery may arrive before the run's workflow_run delivery. Reconcile re-tries linking for unlinked PRs created in the last hour.

## Where the code is

internal/webapi/api.go func webhook (event dispatch); internal/core (new file, e.g. pullrequest.go, with the pure linking function separate from the DB code so it is easy to test); internal/web/server.go and templates.html (`run`, `run-table`, `agent`).

## Dashboard

- Run page: "Pull requests" section: number, title, link to GitHub, opened at, link level badge, findings. No merged/closed state.
- Runs table: an "Outcome" column: "Opened PR #13" (with "inferred" when so); "No PR" only when the run is terminal and no PR is linked; "Unavailable" otherwise. If Jobs show the run's steps after a gate as all skipped, the run page may say so, but keep the Outcome text to the PR fact.
- Deployment page: "Unlinked bot PRs in this repository" with reason and findings.

## Docs

docs/00-glossary.md Escalation row ("Code today" → pull_requests). docs/10-design.md Flow, Data, Trust (PR facts come from signed payloads; links are claims with a level), Limits. docs/20-routes.md webhook and dashboard rows.

## How to check

- Pure unit tests of the linking function for every level and reason (trailer ok; trailer from fork; trailer by human; trailer outside window; no trailer one run; no trailer two runs; no run).
- DB tests: opened adds the PR and an event; a later closed delivery is ignored and changes nothing; PR before run gets linked by Reconcile.
- After deploy and after ag-o6z.6: an audit PR in xpmatteo/rpg-interpreter shows declared on its run; before it, it shows inferred with `missing_trailer`.

## Open questions for Matt

- Should human PRs ever be recorded in Postgres (e.g. a PR that carries a trailer but was opened by a person is recorded today as unlinked/trailer_by_human; other human PRs are not)?

comments.text: From ag-o6z.6 review: .audit/body.md is written by Claude, so the PR body may contain extra or fake 'Agbredo-Run:' lines above the real one. The pipeline's trailer is always the LAST line. Decision for linking: use the last matching trailer line in the body; ignore earlier ones.
2026-10-15: Matt has updated the GitHub App (Pull requests: read, Pull request event subscribed, installations accepted). pull_request deliveries should now arrive.
2026-10-15: Matt said go. Human-PR rule kept: only human PRs carrying a trailer are stored (unlinked, trailer_by_human); other human PRs stay only in the raw archive.

Built on branch ag-o6z.4/bot-prs, commit 05c9129 (not merged, not pushed). Migration 008: pull_requests(id '<repo id>:<number>', owner, repository, number, run_id FK, link CHECK declared/inferred/unlinked, document, updated_at, CHECK unlinked <=> run_id NULL), indexes on run_id and lower(owner),lower(repository). core/pullrequest.go: pure rules (FindTrailer: multiline regex, last match wins, numbers that do not fit -> 0; LinkPullRequest; runWindow = [GitHubStartedAt or CreatedAt, GitHubCompletedAt+60s], open if not finished, no window for a terminal run without completion time). core/pullrequeststore.go: PullRequestWebhook (opened inserts ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING then SELECT FOR UPDATE; edited refreshes title+trailer only of an existing unlinked row; already linked -> ignored), linkAndSave (UPDATE ... WHERE link='unlinked'; event github.pull_request/opened with ID github:pull_request:opened:<delivery that recorded it>, Timestamp = PR created_at), LinkPullRequests (in Reconcile after the poll, errors joined; unlinked PRs created < 1 h ago; DB only; rewrites only when the outcome changes). markHandled/indexDelivery factored out of Webhook. github.ParsePullRequestEvent: shape check (action opened/edited, repository id + owner/name, PR number = payload number <= MaxInt32, user login+type, head ref, created_at, base repo same name (case-insensitive) and same id when given; head repo and body may be null). webapi: pull_request opened/edited -> parse (bad -> 400 failed); other actions ignored before parsing. Choices: (1) a trailer that fails is NEVER inferred instead (its run may be recorded later; an inferred link would lock onto another run). (2) Runs awaiting approval are not inferred candidates (they ran nothing); a declared trailer may still name one. (3) Runs have no repository ID, so 'in this repository' compares names case-insensitively; the repository ID is used for the PR key and the base-repo shape check. (4) 'No PR' only when the run is terminal and started after schema_migrations.applied_at of 008_pull_requests.sql (Fleet.PullRequestsSince); older runs show Unavailable. (5) Deployment page heading 'Unlinked pull requests in this repository' since it also lists trailer_by_human PRs. (6) README: App permission Pull requests: Read and the Pull request event. Tests: pure (trailer cases, every level/reason, window edges, names ignore case, other repo, approval, cap 10 candidates), parser shape, DB (opened links + event; redelivery/closed/reopened/labeled/edited/replay change nothing; recorded or not by repo/author/trailer/deleted/disabled; PR before run linked by Reconcile incl. inferred, old PR not retried; edited adds trailer -> declared, removing it later changes nothing; race of Reconcile+edited+opened -> one link, one event; failure then redelivery), webapi, web. make test passes with DB tests.

Review 2026-10-15, Matt's decisions: (S1) ignore 'edited' deliveries entirely: an editor could add a trailer, forge a declared link and erase findings; the pipeline writes the trailer at opening, so link and findings are decided at opening only. (S2) runs table says 'No PR linked'. (S3) same-repo check before inferring; fork bot PR without valid trailer -> unlinked, reason pr_from_fork. Nits N1,N2(doc),N3,N5,N6,N7,N8 fix now; N4 no action. Open question 'record a PR on edited if opened was lost' answered by S1: no.

title: Record bot PRs and link them to runs: declared, inferred or unlinked, with findings
